note: The canonical feature list. Machine-readable so every client can read it and so a gate can check it, rather than a table that drifts. Validated by website/src/feature-parity.test.ts. See contracts/feature-parity/SKILL.md.

statuses.shipped: Implemented and working on this platform.
statuses.partial: Partly implemented. `gap` says what is missing.
statuses.planned: Specified here, not built on this platform yet.

features.title: The solar system to scale, positioned from real ephemerides
features.why: The product. Everything else hangs off it.

features.title: All 32 bodies: Sun, 8 planets, 23 moons
features.why: A solar system missing Titan and the Galileans is not a true representation.

ios.gap: Sun and 8 planets only. The moons need the mean-element and reference-plane code ported; see contracts/satellite-reference-planes.

features.title: Select and focus any body
features.why: Navigation. Without it the system view is a poster.

ios.gap: The picker selects which body the panel describes, but the camera does not fly to it.

features.title: Body data panel with provenance on every figure
features.why: contracts/numbers-come-from-the-engine. A number without its source is a guess.

ios.gap: Distance, radius and rotation only. Missing axial tilt, temperature, atmosphere, moon count, education facts and declared discrepancies.

features.title: What the clock rate means for the body in view
features.why: "1 day/s" is accurate and tells a viewer nothing. Someone read Earth spinning once a second as a bug.

features.title: Play, pause, reverse, jump to now, and rate presets from real time upward
features.why: Seeing a year pass is the point of a simulator.

features.title: Orbit paths sampled from the solver that positions the body
features.why: An idealised ellipse is decoration. Sampling the real solver draws the path the body will actually follow.

features.title: Real NASA and USGS surface imagery
features.why: A flat tint is a placeholder. The imagery is data too.

features.title: City lights on the dark side, masked by the lighting geometry
features.why: The clearest evidence a simulator can give that the dark side is night rather than empty space.

ios.gap: The texture is already in the bundle. Needs an SCNShaderModifier masked by dot(worldNormal, sunDirection), the SceneKit equivalent of the web's onBeforeCompile.

features.title: Saturn's rings at their real extent, tilted with the planet
features.why: Saturn without rings is not Saturn.

features.title: Day, terminator and night viewing angles
features.why: The thing worth seeing on a planet is usually the line between its day and its night.

features.title: Frame a planet together with its moons
features.why: Framing on the planet alone crops the Moon 1,300 pixels off screen, which reads as a missing Moon.

ios.gap: Needs the moons first; see all-bodies.

features.title: Continuous zoom from system scale to a surface, with a floating origin
features.why: Ten orders of magnitude. contracts/floating-origin.

ios.gap: A fixed divisor is used instead, which is adequate for a system view and will jitter at surface range. renderPosition is the single conversion point so this lands in one function.

features.title: Craters from real elevation data, streamed as tiles
features.why: Real LRO LOLA topography, with the resolution limit stated rather than letting someone conclude the Moon is flat.

features.title: Full N-body mode where every body pulls every other
features.why: The only mode in which a mass you add changes anything. contracts/gravity-modes.

ios.gap: Needs the Dormand-Prince integrator ported to SolarKit.

features.title: Launch an asteroid and propagate it under real gravity
features.why: Where it ends up, with the impact energy, gated against Chelyabinsk, Tunguska and Chicxulub.

features.title: Rocket ascent and payload to orbit
features.why: Inverted gate against ULA's published figures; see the playbook's P7.

features.title: Physics demonstrations, each reproducing a published value
features.why: Kepler's third law, light travel time, solar irradiance, Mercury's relativistic precession.

features.title: Ask about the solar system, answered through engine-backed tools
features.why: contracts/numbers-come-from-the-engine. The model narrates; the engine owns every figure.

ios.gap: Should call the website's /api/ask rather than embedding a key in a shipped binary.

features.title: Star background
features.why: Depth cue, and it should be the real sky.

ios.gap: Randomly placed points rather than a real catalogue. The web builds one from Hipparcos and this should read the same data.

features.title: Orientation from the full IAU rotational elements
features.why: contracts/rotation-and-poles. A sidereal rate alone gives the right speed and the wrong prime meridian.

ios.gap: Spins at the correct sidereal rate and applies the axial tilt, but does not place the prime meridian from W0 and W1, and does not orient to the IAU pole.
